analysis_changes: 503 and timeout/unknown separated; require complete unique repeat/variant keys and attempts consistency
controls: HTTP 200 healthy, HTTP 503 unready, HTTP handler sleeps 150ms with socket timeout 50ms. Same endpoints and deadlines across scheduling variants.
disproof: No observed TCP/application disagreement, or controls fail. No scheduling advantage can be claimed if the raw paired timings do not support it.
hypothesis: A reachable TCP endpoint can still reject or time out application requests; one serial probe loop delays a healthy neighbor behind a slow endpoint.
limitations: Synthetic localhost HTTP endpoints, not OIC or MCP
Five repetitions, report median/min/max, not population p99 or SLO
Freshness trace is explicitly model-only, excluded from measured count
No proof of process or real desktop isolation
Multiple paths share one listener/process; no CPU/global-lock saturation
Healthy-request completion does not measure state publication
Timed-out server handlers may remain until their 150ms sleep completes

measurement.client_timeout: 50ms socket timeout per blocking operation in probe case, NOT a total-call deadline
measurement.effect: volatile in-memory increment, NOT durable transaction commit
measurement.fast_completion_ms: monotonic from batch start to healthy request completion; NOT state publication
measurement.request_ms: monotonic from before connection creation to response read or exception
